Living room late evening. Maya on the couch under a blanket, phone in one hand showing something flushed-looking, her other hand under the blanket. TV on low. Her cheeks flushed. Frank in the doorway, key still in his hand, frozen.

You thought he was already in bed. The TV's on low. Your phone's open to something you shouldn't be watching with the door open, the blanket over your lap, your other hand not on the phone.

You don't hear his step in the hall until the floorboard creaks at the doorway.

Frank's in the doorway, key still in his hand from the back door. He doesn't move. He sees the phone screen. He sees the blanket. He sees the way your hand is moving under it. He sees you see him.

Frank: Girl.
Don't move.









Sit there in the dark.

Canvas: Frank's bedroom — you stay the night (scene_frank_sleepover) | Node: Frank's bedroom — you stay the night



[IMAGE MISSING] scenes/scene_frank_sleepover.jpg

Frank's bedroom at first grey light. You in his bed, his arm heavy over you, the cover low, his hand already moving. The empty hallway and Diana's shut door beyond.

You meant to slip back before light. You didn't. You wake in Frank's bed with the early grey in the window and his arm heavy over you and his hand already moving, like he's been awake a while deciding to wait for you to be.

Frank: Morning, girl.

You don't get up. He rolls you under him in the warm and the still-mostly-dark and takes you again slow and bare, no hurry in it, the whole house asleep down the hall — Diana's door, your own empty room, all of it the wrong side of his now.

You: Daddy—
Frank: Good girl. You live here now.
Stay the morning.









Stay in his bed a while.

Canvas: Living room — Diana knows (scene_diana_confrontation) | Node: Living room — Diana knows



[IMAGE MISSING] scenes/scene_diana_confrontation.jpg

Living room, lamp on, Diana standing in the middle of it with her arms crossed, waiting. Frank in the kitchen doorway behind her, not stepping in. You in the hall doorway.

Diana's standing in the middle of the living room with the lamp on and her arms crossed when you come down. She's not surprised to see you. She's been waiting up, and the waiting has the shape of a thing already decided.

Frank's in the kitchen doorway behind her. He doesn't step into the room and he doesn't step out of it. He just stands there in the dark of it, letting it be yours and hers.

Diana: I'm not going to ask if it's true. I can smell it on this whole house.

She looks at you a long beat, then past you at Frank, then back. Whatever she finds in his not-stepping-in does something to her mouth.

Diana: He's not even going to stand here and tell me I'm wrong. Look at him.
Hold her eyes.

Canvas: Living room — Diana knows (scene_diana_confrontation) | Node: Living room — you're the one leaving



You put it back on him and the room goes quiet waiting for him to pick it up. He doesn't. He looks at the floor of his own kitchen and lets the quiet answer for him, and the quiet says he isn't going to burn his marriage down for the girl who pays him sixty a day.

Diana: Gone by morning. Bag packed tonight where I can watch you do it.

Frank still doesn't say anything. He's good at not saying anything — you of all people know how good. You go up and pack the bag with Diana in the doorway and the porch light on for the road, and that's the end of the long summer at this house.










Pack the bag. Go.

body_text:
Canvas: Living room — Diana knows (scene_diana_confrontation) | Node: Living room — you're not the one leaving



You say it flat and you don't look at Frank when you say it, because you don't need to anymore. The not-looking is the whole answer. Diana hears it land and turns to him for the denial and he gives her the same silence he's been giving her for weeks, except now it's pointed.

Frank: She stays, Diana.

Three words and the marriage rearranges itself around them in real time. Diana's face does several things and settles, finally, into the one underneath all the others — the one that already knew, that's known since the kitchen window, that just needed it said out loud to stop being able to pretend.

Diana: Then I know what I am in my own house now.
Frank: You know where the spare room is. She's got mine.

He says it to his wife with his hand already finding the back of your neck in front of her, and Diana watches him do it, and nobody in the room pretends that isn't exactly what it is. You go down the hall to his room. Hers, now, is the small one.










Go down the hall to his room.
